title: test_inspector shakes the live tree once
intention: test_inspector computes the whole-tree inspect() over the live corpus once and reads that one report for every tooth that judges the live tree, so it seals inside its declared PROOF_TIMEOUT_S of 900s.
why: Measured 2026-11-19: test_inspector timed out at 908s under --reseal and took 1140s under --exec (the orchestrator's runs at cee52402c). After any build_inspector commit its seal stays stale and the component reads red, which blocks the no-iou-wording branch. A stamped run at 4813bb073 took 729.3s idle: tooth 11 311.6s, THE GRADATION 302.6s, ABSENCE 68.6s, every other tooth 7s or less. A per-sieve profile puts one whole inspect() at 277.7s (sole_path_holds 81.9s, a_reached_component_moved 21.5s, intention_fidelity 17.8s). From 2026-10-13 (340s, ticket d48d54dccde6) to now, tickets grew 989 to 3365 (3.4x), proofs 439 to 834 and inspector.py 4200 to 5785 lines. Runtime grew 3.35x, which matches corpus growth, not a regression. The proof runs the same live shake two and a half times.
traces_to: Law 1: the resolver is spent on the novel, not on re-deriving the settled. A second shake of an unchanged tree re-derives a settled report. Law 9: green is earned. A proof that cannot seal inside its own limit leaves its component red for a reason unrelated to the code.
how: In cairn/machines/build_inspector/proofs/test_inspector.py: tooth 11's inspect() binds live_shake; THE GRADATION reads rep = live_shake instead of shaking again; ABSENCE runs its thin, two-sieve pass as _insp.inspect(component='build_inspector') and asserts that the thin gradation is non-empty; a new ONE LIVE SHAKE tooth parses the proof's own source and asserts exactly one inspect() call carries neither root= nor component=. PROOF_TIMEOUT_S stays 900, and its comment records the 2026-11-19 measurement.
